work.title: String Quartet No. 15 in A minor
work.movement: III. Molto adagio (Heiliger Dankgesang); the source’s III–IV combined title is disputed

version.value: Original quartet scoring; movement III. The Archive’s combined III–IV designation is disputed.
version.note: The exact selected 1092.62-second MP3 is retained without truncation or substitution. Its analysed structure supports the five alternating spans of III, at approximately 0, 214, 340, 558 and 686 seconds, followed by slow music through the endpoint. The required report does not establish an A-major march or the IV–V link. Supplementary upper-band inspection finds an F-centred ending; verifier VerH independently checked the selected file’s final37.6s against the score and also found the F ending of III, not IV’s dominant recitative. These are score/audio-feature correspondences, not an aural or complete bar-aligned certification. No IV boundary or IV listening prose is invented. Performing edition, cuts, repeat observance and the completeness of the final played release remain unestablished.

alternatives.value: III–IV combined, as asserted by the Archive filename and catalogue metadata
III only, supported by the selected file’s five-span design and independently checked F-centred endpoint

performers.note: The two photographed disc labels explicitly name all four players and their instruments. They do not label the violin chairs first and second; the dossier does not expand their order into a chair attribution.

date.note: 1952 is the Archive’s catalogue/publication year, not an established session year. The sleeve’s 1951 copyright notice is for the printed package and does not date the session. No dated session ledger or independently matched master history was found in the consulted sources.

place.note: Made in England on the labels establishes manufacture, not recording location. The Archive’s Cebu scan/rip station and the ensemble’s name do not identify a session venue.

label.value: London Records, ffrr long-playing microgroove issue
label.note: London, ffrr and 33⅓ rpm are visible on the labels. The sleeve names The London Gramophone Corporation, New York.

catalogue.note: The Archive and its Discogs-derived catalogue metadata give 1952. The viewed rear sleeve reads Copyright 1951 by The London Gramophone Corporation. A sleeve copyright year is not proof of first sound-recording publication in that year; 1952 is retained as the source’s catalogue year rather than silently resolving the difference. Both are earlier than 1963.

Side 2, label No.2: ABL.598 — movements III, IV and V; the selected digital track is labelled III–IV, but its combined-movement identity is disputed

processing.note: The lineage and ripping-software fields state the hardware/software chain. The side-2 FLAC carries ‘Processed by SoX’; the item’s final segmentation is 7.434–1100.006 seconds of that side capture for III–IV. That is a digital cut range, not score alignment. Stylus calibration beyond the named cartridge, equalisation settings, restoration, de-clicking and pitch/speed correction are not documented; no tuning value is supplied.

digital.format: Internet Archive VBR MP3 derivative (listed average 185 kbps), side-2 segment labelled III–IV; that movement allocation is disputed

composition.value: Underlying composition and the nineteenth-century Breitkopf & Härtel quartet score are public domain.
composition.note: The quartet was composed in 1825; Beethoven died in 1827. The consulted Beethovens Werke engraving, plate B.51, is catalogued as the 1863 edition and Public Domain. This does not clear an unidentified later performing edition or the sleeve author’s prose.

recording.value: Territorial EU public-domain basis only: the recording was published before 1963; US status is not established.
recording.note: The admitted basis is eu-published-before-1963, using the Archive’s 1952 catalogue date for this identified London LLP318 issue. The printed sleeve carries a 1951 copyright notice, corroborating an early-1950s package but not independently establishing the first publication year of the sound recording. A recording published by 1952 had exhausted the ordinary EU 50-year phonogram term before 1 November 2013; the 2011 extension applies to recordings still protected on that date. This is territorial, not a Creative Commons grant or worldwide clearance. The US 1947–1956 term is longer, and no US public-domain claim is made. The Archive item supplies no separate recording licence; availability online and Beethoven’s public-domain composition are not the admission basis.

rights.creditLine: Ludwig van Beethoven, String Quartet No.15, Op.132, III; Archive filename’s III–IV combined designation disputed. The Griller String Quartet. Territorial EU public-domain recording basis; US status unestablished.

sources.title: Selected Griller MP3 — musical-content research
sources.locator: Required report: cache/analysis/beethoven-132-dankgesang.txt, duration1092.6s; boundaries3:34,5:40,9:18,11:26 match III’s five-part design. VerH independently measured the final37.6s in the150–2000Hz band: F predominates at1070–1085s, with chiefly noise by1089s; score printed179 ends III on fermata unison F, whereas IV ends in a dominant recitative. This supports III-only identity without claiming aural review or full score alignment. Provider’s combined title remains disputed.
